pr_body:
Since Kibana's Discover switched to retrieving values via the fields API rather than source there have been gaps in the display caused by "ignored" fields (those that fall foul of ignore_above and ignore_malformed size and formatting rules).

This PR returns ignored values from source when a user-requested field fails to be parsed for a document. In these cases the corresponding hit adds a new ignored_field_values section in the response. The DocumentField class is changed to collect ignored values as well as the valid ones it already did.

Closes #74121
pr_title: Search - return ignored field values from fields api.
pr_comment: @jimczi good to go with this one now?

review_comment: Can we create the unmodifiable list once in the ctr ? We don't do that for the parsed values so that concerns me a bit.
I can make the parsed `values` unmodifiable in the constructor too as part of this change.

Hmm. That currently won't work with the parsed values e.g. [this mutation](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/master/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/search/fetch/subphase/FieldFetcher.java#L262) and [this one](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/master/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/search/fetch/subphase/FetchDocValuesPhase.java#L72)

How do you want to handle this? Live with mutable values for parsed + ignored or change the calling classes like FieldFetcher to use new APIs?
Let's make the ignored values unmodifiable, that's what this PR adds. We can fix the mutable values in a different PR.

Ideally the deserialization logic in the constructor that takes a StreamInput should also create immutable lists rather than plain ArrayLists too. I think I'll save the questions over mutable etc for another PR because clearly we're not going to solve everything here.
